classification.difficultyReason: Use half the square side with the vertical height to find the slant height, then carry that exact value into the base-plus-four-triangles calculation; the parts supply the sequence.

content.prompt: This right square pyramid has base side length $4\text{ m}$ and vertical height $6\text{ m}$.

children.label: a
children.prompt: Find the slant height in exact form.

spec.description: Unshaded right square pyramid with equal base-edge double ticks, a labelled vertical altitude, a perpendicular-height marker and a labelled front base edge. Ordinary source blue edges and red hidden edges become black; the altitude retains semantic red.
spec.mathematics: Square base side 4 m; apex 6 m vertically above the base centre. Explicit faces and viewing direction determine hidden edges. The centre-to-front-edge midpoint construction is separate from solid edges.
spec.answerVisibility: Only supplied measurements appear; the slant height and surface area remain hidden.

answer.worked:
The distance from the base centre to the midpoint of a base edge is $4\div2=2\text{ m}$. Let the slant height be $l$.
$$\begin{aligned}l^2&=6^2+2^2\\l^2&=40\\l&=\sqrt{40}\text{ m}\end{aligned}$$

children.label: b
children.prompt: Find the surface area, correct to 1 d.p.

answer.worked:
Area of base:
$$4\times4=16\text{ m}^2$$
Area of four triangular faces:
$$4\times\left(\frac12\times4\times\sqrt{40}\right)=8\sqrt{40}\text{ m}^2$$
Total surface area:
$$\begin{aligned}A&=16+8\sqrt{40}\\A&\approx66.6\text{ m}^2\end{aligned}$$
